   116	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   117	
   118	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   119	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   120	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   121	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   122	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   123	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   124	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   125	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   126	
   127	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   128	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   129	order
   130	\[
   131	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   132	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   133	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   134	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   135	\]
   136	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   137	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   138	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   139	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   140	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   141	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   142	
   143	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   144	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   145	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   146	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   147	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   148	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   149	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   150	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   151	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   152	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   153	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   154	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   155	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   156	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   157	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   158	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   159	
   160	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   161	\[
   162	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   163	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   164	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   165	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   166	\]
   167	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   168	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   169	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   170	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   171	
   172	The construction theorem is
   173	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   174	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it proves evaluated consistency
   175	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   176	\[
   177	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   178	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   179	\]
   180	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   181	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   182	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   183	pasting argument at lines 942--961 supply the proof. The POVM,
   184	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   185	
   186	The proof conditions the sampling law on the event that the X direction
   187	is nonzero, whose probability lies between $1/2$ and $1$. It leaves the
   188	measurement unchanged. On this event, the polynomial root bound gives the
   189	conditional collision estimate needed for pasting. Multiplication by the
   190	retained probability and addition of the discarded contribution, at most
   191	$1/(2q)$, restore the original product law. Thus the result concerns the
   192	unconditioned X-Z-X measurement, with no conditioning premise in its
   193	statement. The current heterogeneous pasting theorem requires only the two
   194	forward marginal comparisons, both supplied by the point-to-line estimates.
   195	
   196	The directly indexed auxiliary
   197	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} then constructs the point
   198	witness internally, conditions the subline law on each extended line, and
   199	averages the polynomial combination of these actual paired-line effects.
   200	The real-part overlap estimates for both opposite placements give the
   201	corrected bound $C m\,\poly(\eps,md/q)$. This construction retains the
   202	completed answer alphabet and the directly indexed question law; it does not
   203	discharge their comparison with the printed source theorem.\footnote{The
   204	proof and its necessary dependencies were selectively recovered for
   205	\ghissue{512} from commit
   206	\path{6e8d67ef8ba22de69a0c166adcdf23ba6e7a33aa}, retained at
   207	\path{0f4ef05370350f4017439ebd839ef0561f13130f}. See
   208	\path{audits/2026-09-12-issue512-saved-proof-recovery.md} for the
   209	signature audit, axiom closure, and cumulative cost accounting.}
   210	
   211	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   212	
   213	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   214	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   215	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   216	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   217	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   218	\begin{equation}
   219	  \Lambda \,=\,
   220	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   221	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   222	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   223	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   224	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   225	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\textbf{Difficulty.} The domain correction is elementary; the remaining
    22	formal estimate requires the project's state-dependent Cauchy--Schwarz and
    23	restricted-distribution arguments. \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction
    24	affects two Lean modules and their blueprint correspondence. It retains the
    25	unfinished scalar estimate. The pasting consistency construction has been
    26	recovered separately. \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
    27	square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
    28	the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
    29	POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
    30	the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
    31	calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.
    32	
    33	\section{Key theorem forms}
    34	
    35	Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
    36	winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
    37	$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
    38	the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
    39	\begin{align*}
    40	 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
    41	   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
    42	   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
    43	     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
    44	 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
    45	   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
    46	   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
    47	     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
    48	\end{align*}
    49	The paper's Claim 17-2 states
    50	\[
    51	 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
    52	 \quad\text{for}\quad
    53	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
    54	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
    55	\]
    56	The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
    57	with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
    58	combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
    59	independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
    60	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.
    61	
    62	\section{The construction used by the source}
    63	
    64	The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
    65	proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
    66	over the Z polynomial:
    67	\[
    68	 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
    69	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
    70	   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
    71	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
    72	\]
    73	The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
    74	reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
    75	X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
    76	law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
    77	Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
    78	resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
    79	because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
    80	claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
    81	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
    82	labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
    83	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
    84	proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}
    85	
    86	\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}
    87	
    88	Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
    89	The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
    90	$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
    91	$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
    92	players and every line pair, define a POVM by
    93	\[
    94	 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
    95	 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
    96	\]
    97	There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
    98	requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
    99	uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
   100	evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
   101	outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.
   102	
   103	The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
   104	joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
   105	defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
   106	$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
   107	the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
   108	answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
   109	distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
   110	family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
   111	\begin{align*}
   112	 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
   113	 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   114	 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   115	 &=4.
   116	\end{align*}
   117	The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
   118	is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
   119	the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
   120	polynomially small functions of $\eps$.
   121	
   122	For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
   123	\[
   124	 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   125	    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
   126	 \qquad
   127	 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   128	    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
   129	\]
   130	The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
   131	assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
   132	difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
   133	$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
   134	admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
   135	enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
   136	vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.
   137	
   138	\section{Blueprint and formal comparison}
   139	
   140	The concrete measurement domain is retained. The scalar obligation now
   141	compares complex expectations with the complex modulus, preserving the
   142	universal constant, factor $m$, and square-root error. It is named
   143	\leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}. Its distribution is still the
   144	directly indexed law represented by \leanid{SubLineWitness}, not the
   145	source law $D$. Thus it is a formalization-only obligation, linked from
   146	\path{lem:claim-17-2-direct}, and is not a formalization of the source
   147	claim. The source statement remains at \path{lem:claim-17-2}, with neither
   148	a Lean link nor a completion mark.
   149	
   150	The same scalar distinction affects Claim 17-1: an ordered product
   151	$M^Z_bM^X_a$ need not be Hermitian, so a bound on the real part of its
   152	correlation does not bound its complex modulus. The proved real-part
   153	estimate is retained as
   154	\leanid{subline\_replace\_by\_ordered\_product\_re\_direct}.
   155	Its constant is $2\sqrt{\delta_Q}$: the squared-distance comparison on
   156	one placement is $4\delta_Q$ and uses $W^\dagger W$, not $W^2$.
   157	The source Claim 17-1 remains a separate uncertified blueprint statement.
   158	Likewise \leanid{subline\_Z\_term\_near\_one\_re\_direct} retains the
   159	proved real Z-overlap estimate with its directly indexed domain explicit.
   160	No reality or distribution-transport theorem is asserted by these renamings.
   161	The three existing source blueprint statements are reused; no duplicate
   162	source theorem with a new proof hole is introduced.
   163	
   164	The distribution discrepancy is documented in
   165	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}. Admissibility
   166	does not supply the divisibility needed to instantiate the source line law
   167	at dimension $2m+2$. The current correction neither adds that divisibility
   168	as a hypothesis nor identifies the directly indexed law with the source law.
   169	Scalar realignment is tracked in \ghissue{474} and review of PR~478.
   170	The distribution and complex-overlap work under \ghissue{118} remains open;
   171	its historical budget is unchanged.
   172	
   173	The abstract combined-line witness record remains unchanged. Its fields
   174	faithfully express the existential conclusion of the combined-lines lemma,
   175	but do not characterize the construction used in its proof. The internal
   176	consistency obligation now refers to the concrete sandwich. Both witness
   177	existence proofs construct their records with that measurement. A later
   178	argument needing the exact construction can use the consistency obligation
   179	and the same explicit record; merely choosing an unspecified existential
   180	witness does not recover its defining formula.\footnote{The Lean-only
   181	theorem is \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency} in
   182	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/Construction.lean}. Its hypotheses explicitly supply
   183	a polynomially controlled point family. Its proof was recovered for
   184	\ghissue{512} from the saved point-to-line comparisons and pasting argument,
   185	including restoration of discarded zero-direction probability. The source-facing
   186	\leanid{exists\_combinedLinesWitness} has an unchanged statement.}
   187	
   188	The retained direct proof hole in these two modules is
   189	\leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}: apply complex
   190	weighted Cauchy--Schwarz to bound $|A(T)-B(T)|$ by the square root of the
   191	X-overlap deficit, then use the already proved
   192	\leanid{exists\_concreteXPointOverlap\_deficit\_le}. That estimate already
   193	uses \leanid{combinedLineMeasurement\_sum\_Z}, expanded line-point
   194	consistency, and the separate X marginal of the directly indexed law.
   195	Transport of this argument and of the real-part estimates to the source
   196	law, including the complex estimate of Claim 17-1, is a separate remaining
   197	obligation. No additional hole is introduced for that transport.
   198	
   199	The recovered theorem \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency}
   200	proves consistency of the same unconditioned X-Z-X measurement
   201	with the supplied polynomially controlled joint point family on the
   202	original product of line-point distributions, in every opposite placement.
   203	The construction and its discharge by the source point-to-line comparison and
   204	pasting argument are described in
   205	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex}.
   206	No marginal identity, deficit bound, or producer is added to a paper theorem.
   207	
   208	\section{Conclusion}
   209	
   210	The discrepancy lies in the formal quantification over arbitrary witnesses,
   211	not in the paper's constructed-measurement assertion. The counterexample
   212	forces a domain correction. Using the defined sandwich restores the measurement domain. The complex
   213	scalar conclusion is restored for the directly indexed auxiliary obligation;
   214	its complex proof and transport to the source distribution remain
   215	open. The source claims themselves retain their complex-modulus statements
   216	without unsupported formalization marks.

   882		Let $K$ be a finite integral domain, let $c\in\N$, and let
   883		$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
   884		$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$
   885		agree at at most $c$ elements of $K$.
   886		The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
   887		and has natural degree at most $c$.
   888		This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step
   889		in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
   890		(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:955}).
   891		There is no restriction $c<|K|$.
   892	\end{lemma}
   893	\begin{proof}
   894		\leanok
   895		The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
   896		and gives polynomials of degree at most $c$. If the polynomials agreed
   897		at more than $c$ elements, the univariate root bound applied to their
   898		difference would force them to be equal, contradicting $f\ne g$.

1	---
     2	title: Audit document format
     3	date: 2026-04-29
     4	purpose: >
     5	  Defines the audit-file naming, YAML front matter, terminology, and review
     6	  use conventions for MIPStarRE audit documents.
     7	status: active
     8	track: documentation
     9	kind: audit-format
    10	origin: "issue #913"
    11	issue: "#913"
    12	pr: "#915"
    13	---
    14	
    15	# Audit Document Format
    16	
    17	This file gives the common format and terminology for audit documents under
    18	`audits/`. Every audit file should begin with YAML front matter. New audit
    19	files and substantive updates to existing audits should also follow the section
    20	format below.
    21	
    22	## Metadata
    23	
    24	Every audit should begin with YAML front matter in this shape:
    25	
    26	```yaml
    27	---
    28	title: "Short human-readable title"
    29	date: YYYY-MM-DD
    30	purpose: >
    31	  One or two sentences explaining what the audit records and how it should be
    32	  used by later readers.
    33	---
    34	```
    35	
    36	Use `issue` and `pr` when the audit is tied to a specific GitHub issue or pull
    37	request:
    38	
    39	```yaml
    40	issue: "#N"
    41	pr: "#M"
    42	```
    43	
    44	The values should be quoted strings such as `"#913"` so YAML parses them as
    45	text rather than comments.
    46	
    47	Existing or useful classification fields may be kept. In this repository the
    48	common ones are:
    49	
    50	```yaml
    51	status: active
    52	track: paper2009ldt
    53	kind: naming-audit
    54	origin: internal
    55	```
    56	
    57	These fields are optional metadata, not a replacement for the prose purpose.
    58	When adding a new audit, prefer the minimal header above unless the extra fields
    59	help later readers sort or review the audit.
    60	
    61	## File Names
    62	
    63	Dated audit artifacts should use a leading `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename. For example,
    64	use `2026-04-29_mathematical-naming-audit.md`, not
    65	`mathematical-naming-audit_2026-04-29.md` and not
    66	`20260429_mathematical-naming-audit.md`.
    67	
    68	## Required Sections
    69	
    70	Use these sections unless the audit is deliberately narrower:
    71	
    72	- `Scope`: the files, declarations, prose, or mathematical objects audited.
    73	- `Source of Truth`: the paper, blueprint chapter, or repository convention used
    74	  to decide the mathematical terminology.
    75	- `Findings`: the observed mismatches, grouped by mathematical topic or API
    76	  surface.
    77	- `Required Action`: the precise cleanup or migration needed before the audit
    78	  can be marked resolved.
    79	- `Validation`: the Lean, blueprint, or documentation checks relevant to the
    80	  audit.
    81	- `Review Use`: how reviewers should apply the audit in later PRs.
    82	
    83	## Term Norm
    84	
    85	Audit prose should use terms from the mathematical source, the blueprint, or an
    86	established repository convention. It should not introduce project management
    87	phrases as mathematical names. In particular, avoid presenting words such as
    88	`pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as preferred
    89	mathematical terminology unless the cited source uses them with that meaning.
    90	
    91	When an audit names a problematic existing identifier, describe it as a legacy
    92	identifier or a finding. Do not turn an implementation-history word into the
    93	title of a new concept. Prefer terms such as:
    94	
    95	- `finding`
    96	- `required action`
    97	- `legacy identifier`
    98	- `source of truth`
    99	- `validation`
   100	- `review use`
   101	- `API migration`
   102	
   103	For Lean naming audits, a name is suspect when it encodes historical
   104	formalization status rather than mathematical content. If a public name cannot
   105	be changed immediately, record the migration here or in a linked issue, and do
   106	not add an empty pass-through abbreviation just to create a second public name.
   107	
   108	## Review Rule
   109	
   110	When a review fix touches a surface covered by an active audit, the audit is
   111	required reading. A PR is not ready to merge if it ignores an in-scope required
   112	action, leaves the same terminology problem on the touched surface, or replaces
   113	it only with an empty pass-through abbreviation. If the PR deliberately defers
   114	the migration, it should update the audit or linked issue with the remaining
   115	work and the mathematical reason for the deferral.

1	\documentclass[11pt]{article}

     3	\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
     4	\usepackage{xurl}
     5	\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
     6	\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
     7

     9	
    10	\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}
    11	\author{}
    12	\date{2026-04-29}
    13	
    14	\begin{document}
    15	\maketitle
    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
   112	replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
   113	which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
   114	then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
   115	Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
   116	Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
   117	than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
   118	availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
   119	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
   120	definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
   121	inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.
   122	
   123	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   124	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   125	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   126	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   127	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   128	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   129	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   130	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   131	implementation.
   132	
   133	\section{When to Write a Note}
   134	
   135	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   136	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   137	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   138	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   139	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   140	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   141	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   142	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   143	relation.
   144	
   145	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   146	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   147	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   148	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   149	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   150	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   151	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   152	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   153	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   154	
   155	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   156	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   157	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   158	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   159	
   160	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   161	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   162	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   163	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   164	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   165	though it were the paper theorem.
   166	
   167	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   168	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   169	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   170	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   171	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   172	argument.
   173	
   174	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   175	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   176	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   177	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   178	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   179	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   180	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   181	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   182	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   183	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   184	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   185	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   186	
   187	\section{Counterexamples}
   188	
   189	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   190	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   191	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   192	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   193	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   194	
   195	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   196	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   197	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   198	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   199	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   200	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   201	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   202	
   203	\section{Revision of a Note}
   204	
   205	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   206	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   207	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   208	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   209	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   210	which point remains unsettled.
   211	
   212	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   213	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   214	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   215	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   216	discussion.
   217	
   218	\section{Form of the Note}
   219	
   220	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
   221	source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
   222	original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
   223	be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
   224	recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
   225	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
   226	around the mathematical assertion and its proof.
   227	
   228	The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
   229	measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
   230	should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
   231	state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
   232	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   233	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   234	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.
   235	
   236	Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
   237	substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
   238	a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
   239	proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
   240	logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

+/-- Indicator averages express the positive-fiber collision predicate of
+`lem:pasting`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
+This formalization-only adapter is applied below with a proved fiber estimate. -/
+theorem collision_bound_of_fiber_averages {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
+    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
+    [Fintype Γ₂] (dist : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
+    (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂) (eta : ℝ)
+    (hbound : ∀ fixed : X × Y₁, ∀ first second : Γ₂, first ≠ second →
+      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then
+        (if eval₂ first sample.2 = eval₂ second sample.2 then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
+      eta * avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then 1 else 0)) :
+    HasConditionalCollisionBound dist eval₂ eta := by
+  classical
+  intro question point _ first second hne
+  have havg (value : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → ℝ) :
+      avgOver dist value = ∑ sample, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
+    exact (dist.sum_univ_eq_sum_support _ (fun sample hout => by
+      rw [dist.outsideSupport sample hout, zero_mul])).symm
+  have hmass : (dist.map Prod.fst).weight (question, point) =
+      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = (question, point) then 1 else 0) := by
+    rw [Distribution.map_weight, Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver]
+  rw [hmass]
+  have h := hbound (question, point) first second hne
+  simpa [havg, Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_ite] using h

+theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}

+        (if evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 first =
+          evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 second then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
+    (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
+      avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
+        if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 else 0) := by
+  classical
+  simp only [avgOver_prod]
+  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)

+  apply avgOver_mono
+  intro sample

+/-- Proof-only question law for one-sided pasting in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper

+`(((sX.line,sZ.line),sZ),sX)`. Thus `G1 = Z` and `G2 = X`; the evaluation

+    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×

+  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))
+    (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0)
+    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map
+      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))

+/-- The actual conditioned product question law satisfies the conditional
+collision predicate with parameter `bound/q`. This discharges, rather than

+proof-only; the discarded probability remains in the restoration estimate. -/
+theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_collision_bound (P : AdmissibleParams) (bound : ℕ) :
+    HasConditionalCollisionBound (nondegenerateLinePastingDist P.toLdParams)

+  have hswap (condition other : Prop) [Decidable condition] [Decidable other] (value : ℝ) :
